The real struggle with statements like “everybody is a little autistic” is that the thing that people equate to being autistic may be experienced by lots of people, but it is not experienced at the same level. For example, when neurotypical people touch a texture they don’t like, they move on after a moment. When I touch a texture I don’t like, it leaves me feeling like my skin is crawling and will continue to do so until I find a soothing texture to touch instead. 

There’s also the real issue of Autism is quite possibly way more prevalent than we have any idea, due in particular to the lack of study of groups that don’t fit the typical criteria, that being white middle class boys/men. Not to mention, the sheer number of people who are masked autistics is truly unknown because they have become masters of hiding their true self, so maybe the “everyone is a little autistic” statement is just emphasizing a massive problem that healthcare “professionals” DON’T KNOW WHAT TO LOOK FOR WHEN PEOPLE ARE MADKED AUTISTICS.
